stem: Where is Hirschsprung disease usually located?
explanation: Rectosigmoid level is the usual site of Hirschsprung disease.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Additional Congenital Surgical Problems

optionExplanations.A: Correct because Hirschsprung disease usually involves aganglionosis at the rectosigmoid level.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because Hirschsprung disease does not usually present as an isolated stomach lesion.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Hirschsprung disease affects the distal bowel, not the mid-oesophagus.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because Hirschsprung disease is not usually located in the jejunum only.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because Hirschsprung disease is due to bowel aganglionosis, not an isolated anal sphincter problem.

sourceRefs: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
